ui.subtitle: Exploring how data visualizations shape our perception
ui.description: An interactive research tool for detecting potentially misleading data visualizations.
ui.header_only: This CSV has column headers but no data rows. Add observations before building a chart.
ui.numeric_required: Your CSV file must contain at least one numeric column.
ui.box_group_note: Leave this as All observations for one overall distribution. For grouped boxes, choose a column with repeated group values.
ui.two_columns: Choose a dataset with at least two columns to build a chart.
ui.no_usable_rows: No rows have usable values for the selected chart.
ui.exclude_histogram: Rows with missing or non-finite histogram values are excluded.
ui.exclude_box_all: Rows with missing or non-finite Y values are excluded.
ui.exclude_xy: Rows missing X or Y, and non-finite Y values, are excluded.
ui.custom_range: Set a custom {axis} range for the original chart
ui.range_error: The Y-axis minimum must be smaller than its maximum.
ui.sorted_line: The corrected line chart orders {kind} X values from low to high.
ui.scale_bar: The scale includes all observed values and zero, so bar lengths share a meaningful baseline.
ui.scale_histogram: The X-axis includes the full observed value range so the histogram does not hide bins.
ui.scale_other: The scale shows the full observed data range with a small margin.
ui.export_original_error: Could not export the original chart: {error}
ui.export_recommended_error: Could not export the recommended chart: {error}

bar_axis_integrity.title: Bar-chart baseline and data range
bar_axis_integrity.explanation: The check compares the displayed Y-axis with the observed values and zero.
bar_axis_integrity.impact: Clipping values can hide observations; omitting zero can make bar differences look larger.
bar_axis_integrity.limitations: A non-zero baseline is a review signal, not proof of misleading intent. The check does not account for domain-specific reasons to zoom the scale.
bar_axis_integrity.recommendation_detected: Expand the range to include all observed values and zero.
bar_axis_integrity.recommendation_clear: No axis correction is needed for the selected settings.
bar_axis_integrity.recommendation_not_applicable: No baseline change is recommended by this bar-specific check.
bar_axis_integrity.evidence_no_values: No finite numeric Y values were supplied.
bar_axis_integrity.evidence_auto: Observed data range: {data_min} to {data_max}; no custom axis bounds were supplied.
bar_axis_integrity.evidence_custom: Observed data: {data_min} to {data_max}. Selected Y-axis: {axis_min} to {axis_max}.{clip}{zero}
bar_axis_integrity.clip: At least one observed value falls outside the selected axis range.
bar_axis_integrity.zero: The selected axis range excludes zero.

axis_data_visibility.title: {axis} data visibility
axis_data_visibility.explanation: The check compares the selected {axis} range with all finite plotted values.
axis_data_visibility.impact_line: Clipping line or scatter values can hide points or parts of a trend.
axis_data_visibility.impact_box: Clipping Y values can hide whiskers, outliers, or parts of a box-plot distribution.
axis_data_visibility.impact_histogram: Clipping X values can hide observations or remove histogram bins.
axis_data_visibility.limitations: This check evaluates axis bounds created in the app. It does not inspect an imported chart image.
axis_data_visibility.recommendation_detected: Expand the {axis} range to include all observed values.
axis_data_visibility.recommendation_clear: No {axis} range correction is needed for the selected settings.
axis_data_visibility.recommendation_not_applicable: There are no finite chart values to assess.
axis_data_visibility.evidence_no_values: No finite numeric chart values were supplied.
axis_data_visibility.evidence_auto: Observed data range: {data_min} to {data_max}; the chart uses an automatic {axis} range.
axis_data_visibility.evidence_custom: Observed data range: {data_min} to {data_max}. Selected {axis}: {axis_min} to {axis_max}.{clip_low}{clip_high}
axis_data_visibility.clip_low: Values below the axis minimum are clipped.
axis_data_visibility.clip_high: Values above the axis maximum are clipped.

difference_amplification.title: Estimated visual amplification
difference_amplification.explanation: The estimate compares the ratio of visible bar lengths with the ratio of the underlying positive values.
difference_amplification.impact: A truncated baseline may make the largest value appear disproportionately larger.
difference_amplification.limitations: The estimate only applies to positive values, at least two distinct categories, a fully visible data range, and a baseline below the smallest value.
difference_amplification.recommendation_detected: Include zero in the Y-axis range and compare the resulting chart.
difference_amplification.recommendation_not_applicable: Use a zero baseline or compare the chart with the recommended view.
difference_amplification.evidence_not_bar: No numeric estimate is available for the selected settings.
difference_amplification.evidence_one_category: Only one distinct X category is available, so a between-category difference cannot be quantified.
difference_amplification.evidence_nonpositive: The data include zero or negative values, or all values are equal; a positive-value ratio is undefined or uninformative.
difference_amplification.evidence_clipped: The selected axis clips the data, so comparing displayed and true bar-length ratios would be misleading.
difference_amplification.evidence_zero: The displayed bars use a zero baseline; estimated amplification is 1.00×.
difference_amplification.evidence_estimate: Data ratio: {data_ratio}×. Displayed bar-length ratio: {displayed_ratio}×. Estimated relative amplification: {factor}×.
difference_amplification.evidence_unstable: The values are too extreme for a stable finite amplification estimate.
difference_amplification.evidence_unavailable: No numeric estimate is available for the selected settings.

incomplete_rows.title: Rows omitted from the chart
incomplete_rows.impact: Omitted rows can change how complete or representative the chart appears.
incomplete_rows.limitations: This check reports row counts; it does not infer why values are missing.
incomplete_rows.recommendation_detected: Review the affected rows and decide whether to correct, exclude, or explain them.
incomplete_rows.recommendation_clear: No action is needed for missing chart values.
incomplete_rows.evidence_histogram: {count} row(s) were excluded because the histogram value is missing or non-finite.
incomplete_rows.evidence_histogram_clear: No rows were excluded for missing or non-finite histogram values.
incomplete_rows.explanation_histogram: A histogram needs a finite numeric value for each included row.
incomplete_rows.evidence_box_all: {count} row(s) were excluded because the Y value is missing or non-finite.
incomplete_rows.evidence_box_all_clear: No rows were excluded for missing or non-finite Y values.
incomplete_rows.explanation_box_all: A box plot needs a finite numeric Y value for each included observation.
incomplete_rows.evidence_xy: {count} row(s) were excluded because X or Y is missing, or Y is not finite.
incomplete_rows.evidence_xy_clear: No rows were excluded for missing X or invalid Y values.
incomplete_rows.explanation_xy: The chart requires a usable X value and a finite numeric Y value for each point.

line_x_order.title: Line-chart X order
line_x_order.explanation: The check compares file order with numeric or date order before connecting points.
line_x_order.impact: Connecting points in a different order can imply a false sequence or trend.
line_x_order.limitations: Sorting only applies when every X value is consistently numeric or date-like; categorical sequence may carry its own meaning.
line_x_order.recommendation_detected: Use the sorted comparison chart or sort the source rows before interpreting the trend.
line_x_order.recommendation_clear: No ordering change is recommended by this check.
line_x_order.recommendation_not_applicable: The order could not be inferred safely from the selected X values.
line_x_order.evidence_not_sortable: X values are not consistently numeric or date-like, so order cannot be inferred safely.
line_x_order.evidence_unsorted: The original line connects numeric or date-like X values in file order, not sorted order.
line_x_order.evidence_sorted: Numeric or date-like X values are already in ascending order.

chart_data_suitability.title: Chart and data suitability
chart_data_suitability.explanation: The check looks for constant Y values and, for bar charts, a large number of categories.
chart_data_suitability.impact: Constant values may not show a meaningful comparison; many bars can make labels and differences hard to read.
chart_data_suitability.limitations: More than {threshold} bar categories is a review heuristic, not a universal limit. The check does not know the user's question or domain conventions.
chart_data_suitability.recommendation_detected: Check whether this chart answers the intended question. For many categories, consider a focused subset or a clearly explained grouping; do not discard values silently.
chart_data_suitability.recommendation_clear: No issue was found by these basic suitability checks.
chart_data_suitability.recommendation_not_applicable: Add observations before interpreting a pattern or distribution.
chart_data_suitability.evidence_empty: No finite numeric Y values were supplied.
chart_data_suitability.evidence_detected_constant: All finite Y values are identical.
chart_data_suitability.evidence_detected_crowded: The bar chart has {categories} categories (review threshold: more than {threshold}).
chart_data_suitability.evidence_single: Only one finite Y value is available.
chart_data_suitability.evidence_clear: {distinct} distinct finite Y values are available.{categories_note}

repeated_categories.title: Repeated bar-chart categories
repeated_categories.explanation: The check counts repeated X categories in the rows used to build the bar chart.
repeated_categories.impact: Plotly draws a bar for each row; repeated X values can overlap instead of showing a category total.
repeated_categories.limitations: Repeated categories may be intentional. This check does not infer the correct aggregation rule.
repeated_categories.recommendation_detected: Choose and state an aggregation rule, such as sum or mean, or use a chart that preserves individual observations. The app does not aggregate automatically.
repeated_categories.recommendation_not_applicable: This check applies to bar charts with X values.
repeated_categories.evidence_detected: {duplicates} duplicate row(s) occur across {repeated} repeated category value(s), among {rows} plotted rows.
repeated_categories.evidence_clear: All {rows} plotted rows have distinct X categories.

extreme_value_context.title: Potentially influential extreme values
extreme_value_context.explanation: The screen uses 3×IQR fences and checks whether the full range is at least 10× the IQR.
extreme_value_context.impact: A scale-dominating value can compress variation among the other observations.
extreme_value_context.limitations: This is a statistical review signal, not proof of an error or misleading intent. Valid domain values may be extreme; the check does not inspect their meaning.
extreme_value_context.recommendation_detected: Verify the extreme observations and provide context. Consider annotation or a separate view; do not remove values automatically.
extreme_value_context.recommendation_clear: No scale-dominating extreme-value signal was found by this screen.
extreme_value_context.recommendation_not_applicable: At least five usable values with non-zero spread are needed for this screen.
extreme_value_context.evidence_few: Only {count} finite value(s) are available; at least 5 are needed for this screen.
extreme_value_context.evidence_iqr: The interquartile range is zero or non-finite, so relative scale influence cannot be estimated.
extreme_value_context.evidence_result: {outliers} value(s) fall beyond the 3×IQR fences; the full data range is {ratio}× the IQR.
extreme_value_context.evidence_ratio_overflow: {outliers} value(s) fall beyond the 3×IQR fences; the full data range exceeds the finite IQR ratio.
